react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-analysis paradigms converge on a single dominant biological theme: systemic perturbation of androgen and estrogen metabolism. RaMP-DB multi-database ORA returned KEGG:map00140 "Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism" at rank 2 with FDR = 2.93e-15 and fold-enrichment = 1668, hitting all five steroid hormones (estrone, dehydroepiandrosterone, testosterone, estradiol, 17β-hydroxy-5α-androstan-3-one). The same pathway appeared as SMPDB:SMP00068 (rank 1) and SMPDB:SMP00356 (rank 0), both with identical FDR and fold-enrichment, and as Reactome R-HSA-196071 "Metabolism of steroid hormones" at rank 4 (FDR = 1.67e-14). MetaboAnalystR KEGG-specific PSEA confirmed KEGG:hsa00140 at rank 0 (p = 2.51e-06) with the same five steroid metabolites. Mummichog m/z-direct activity against the human_mfn empirical network placed "Androgen and estrogen biosynthesis and metabolism" at rank 0 (p = 8.40e-05), with all five input steroids present among the 11 pathway members, producing a perfect overlap (11/11). The sixth input, guanidoacetic acid, appeared only in weaker Mummichog pathways (glycine/serine/alanine metabolism, urea cycle) with p > 0.05 and is not a driver. N-Acetylgalactosamine mapped to N-acetyl-D-glucosamine and surfaced only in minor glycosaminoglycan pathways (hyaluronan, sialic acid) with p > 0.05, also below significance. Estrone, DHEA, testosterone, estradiol, and dihydrotestosterone therefore constitute the core driver set, collectively implicating the steroidogenesis axis as the primary affected pathway across ORA, KEGG-specific PSEA, and network-diffusion (m/z) paradigms. The direction of change (up or down) was not specified; the study captures differential abundance but the consensus signal is a coordinated perturbation of the C18/C19 steroid pool consistent with altered aromatase or hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase activity.

final_react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-analysis paradigms converge on a single dominant biological theme: systemic perturbation of androgen and estrogen metabolism. RaMP-DB multi-database ORA returned KEGG:map00140 "Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism" at rank 2 with FDR = 2.93e-15 and fold-enrichment = 1668, hitting all five steroid hormones (estrone, dehydroepiandrosterone, testosterone, estradiol, 17β-hydroxy-5α-androstan-3-one). The same pathway appeared as SMPDB:SMP00068 (rank 1) and SMPDB:SMP00356 (rank 0), both with identical FDR and fold-enrichment, and as Reactome R-HSA-196071 "Metabolism of steroid hormones" at rank 4 (FDR = 1.67e-14). MetaboAnalystR KEGG-specific PSEA confirmed KEGG:hsa00140 at rank 0 (p = 2.51e-06) with the same five steroid metabolites. Mummichog m/z-direct activity against the human_mfn empirical network placed "Androgen and estrogen biosynthesis and metabolism" at rank 0 (p = 8.40e-05), with all five input steroids present among the 11 pathway members, producing a perfect overlap (11/11). The sixth input, guanidoacetic acid, appeared only in weaker Mummichog pathways (glycine/serine/alanine metabolism, urea cycle) with p > 0.05 and is not a driver. N-Acetylgalactosamine mapped to N-acetyl-D-glucosamine and surfaced only in minor glycosaminoglycan pathways (hyaluronan, sialic acid) with p > 0.05, also below significance. Estrone, DHEA, testosterone, estradiol, and dihydrotestosterone therefore constitute the core driver set, collectively implicating the steroidogenesis axis as the primary affected pathway across ORA, KEGG-specific PSEA, and network-diffusion (m/z) paradigms. The direction of change (up or down) was not specified; the study captures differential abundance but the consensus signal is a coordinated perturbation of the C18/C19 steroid pool consistent with altered aromatase or hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase activity.
